entities.name: ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Assembly
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA), established in 1977 as the ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Organisation (AIPO) and renamed in 2007, is the inter-parliamentary body of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) — a consultative forum bringing together the national parliaments of ASEAN's 10 member states (Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia) to promote parliamentary cooperation, regional integration, and democratic governance across Southeast Asia.

AIPA operates in a uniquely challenging context among inter-parliamentary bodies: its membership includes both multi-party democracies (Philippines, Indonesia), constitutional monarchies with limited pluralism (Thailand, Malaysia), quasi-one-party states (Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam, Singapore's quasi-competitive system), and a military junta (Myanmar, which ASEAN suspended following the 2021 coup). This diversity of political systems means AIPA must balance advocacy for democratic governance with ASEAN's foundational 'non-interference' principle.

The body has no legislative power — it issues statements, resolutions, and recommendations that are not binding on ASEAN governments. However, it has become increasingly active on issues including anti-corruption, human rights, environmental governance, and women's empowerment. The most consequential recent challenge has been Myanmar: AIPA suspended Myanmar's parliament (Pyidaungsu Hluttaw) following the February 2021 military coup and has navigated the tension between ASEAN principles of non-interference and the international community's expectation that regional bodies respond to military takeovers of democratic governments.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: AIPA — the inter-parliamentary body of 10 Southeast Asian nations covering 680+ million people, navigating democratic governance advocacy amid ASEAN's non-interference principle, and making the consequential decision to suspend Myanmar after its 2021 military coup — is a significant institution in Southeast Asian regional integration.
